findings.title: The `import()` calls run as soon as the module loads, so nothing is loaded lazily
findings.body: Every property in this object literal is an `import("./x")` expression. Each one is evaluated, and starts loading its app, at the moment `@calcom/app-store` is first imported. All 28 apps still load on every cold start, whether or not the request uses them. The only difference from the static imports is that callers now have to `await`. To defer loading until an app is actually requested, store thunks instead (`applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`) and call them at the lookup sites: `getCalendar.ts:15`, `videoClient.ts:26`, `handlePayment.ts:26`, `deletePayment.ts:16`, `handleCancelBooking.ts:589` and `bookings.tsx:967`. A side effect of the eager version: an app module that fails to load produces a rejected promise that nothing handles until some request happens to look that app up.

findings.title: `forEach(async …)` means the surrounding try/catch no longer catches errors from `getCalendar`
findings.body: `getCalendar` is now async. Before, an exception thrown while building the CalendarService (inside `getCalendar`) was synchronous and reached the `catch` at line 135, which logged it. Now it rejects the promise returned by the async `forEach` callback, and that promise is discarded. The `catch` cannot see it, so the error becomes an unhandled rejection and is never logged through `logger`. The same pattern is in `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125` and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:553`; in bookings.tsx there is no try/catch at all. The `deleteEvent` and `deleteMeeting` promises were already fire-and-forget before this change. Collecting the promises with `map` and putting `await Promise.allSettled(...)` inside the try would restore the logging and also wait for the deletions before the reschedule emails are sent.

contracts.action: getCalendarCredentials now stores a Promise<Calendar|null> in `calendar`, and getConnectedCalendars awaits it
contracts.before_after: Every caller passes the result straight into getConnectedCalendars. None of them reads `.calendar` directly, and getConnectedCalendars awaits it inside its try (line 48).
contracts.visible_effect: The connected-calendars list in settings and the availability API look the same as before.
contracts.failure_mode: If getCalendar rejects, the error is caught at CalendarManager.ts:94 and that entry is returned with an error message. Before, a synchronous throw escaped getCalendarCredentials.

contracts.action: appStore values become promises from import(), awaited at every lookup site
contracts.equivalent_path: Every `appStore[...]` lookup in the repository: getCalendar.ts:15, videoClient.ts:26, handlePayment.ts:26, deletePayment.ts:16, handleCancelBooking.ts:589, bookings.tsx:967
contracts.before_after: Every lookup site found by grep now awaits the value. An unknown key such as an undefined dirName gives undefined, and awaiting undefined is still undefined, so the `"lib" in` guards behave as before.
contracts.visible_effect: No visible change. All modules still load when the app-store module is imported.
contracts.failure_mode: An app module that fails to import leaves a rejected promise that nothing handles until a lookup awaits it.

contracts.action: Request-reschedule deletes calendar events inside a forEach(async) callback
contracts.equivalent_path: handleCancelBooking.ts:229-277 collects its delete promises and awaits Promise.all
contracts.before_after: The cancel path awaits its deletions before updating the booking. The reschedule paths fire the deletions and move straight on to sending emails.
contracts.visible_effect: Emails go out whether or not the calendar deletions succeeded.
contracts.failure_mode: A rejection from getCalendar is unhandled and never logged (the vital and wipemycalother try/catch blocks no longer catch it).

summary: The PR turns the app-store map into dynamic `import()` promises and makes `getCalendar` and `getVideoAdapters` async. Every lookup site and caller found by grep now awaits correctly, so nothing should behave differently at runtime. However, the imports are evaluated eagerly in the object literal, so no app is actually loaded lazily. In three reschedule paths, `forEach(async)` lets errors from `getCalendar` escape their try/catch.
